column7: A two-gain-stage fuzz/driver with three highly interactive switching controls. The builder presents it as an original design rather than a direct recreation of another famous fuzz circuit; contemporary 2024 coverage emphasizes its mid-gain, textured and saturating range.
column10: Strong external clues are the three interactive toggles, compact 29 Pedals format and the overlap between mid-gain overdrive and fuzz. Keep it separate from the FLWR despite shared control topology.

column7: A broad-range gain pedal spanning boost, overdrive, distortion and fuzz territory, described by Premier Guitar as capable of many shades across the gain spectrum while retaining a smooth, creamy fuzz character.
column10: Treat the broad gain range as an identification characteristic, not a reason to collapse Nectar into a generic fuzz record. Preserve the Beetronics product identity and 2024 release context.

column7: Modern fuzz/processing design selected among GPX's 2024 finalists. Its title and contemporary coverage place it in the octave/experimental fuzz branch rather than a straightforward vintage recreation.
column10: Primary builder documentation should be added before promoting detailed architecture or generation claims. Preserve the 2024 finalist record as a discovery anchor.

column7: A highly configurable classic-fuzz platform using three selected silicon transistors, with Fuzz Face and Tone Bender territory plus harmonic-octave and oscillation possibilities. Seven controls and three footswitches form a major part of its specimen identity.
column10: Preserve Lütz as an original Horrothia product rather than labeling it a Fuzz Face or Tone Bender clone. Control layout, filter sections, Bias and Cap Defeat are high-value identification clues.

column7: A mostly op-amp Fuzz Face-style fuzz blended with Cornerstone's Gladio-style Dumble overdrive section. Volume, Gain, Comp, Tone and dual Bias controls define a broad fuzz-to-overdrive range.
column10: Keep the Gladio relationship as lineage/collaboration context, not as product identity. The dual-bias architecture and blend behavior are useful specimen clues.

column7: Danelectro product designed around Steve Ridinger's 1960s concept, offering Fuzz, Drive, Volume and Tone plus a two-position voicing switch. Contemporary launch coverage describes its range from searing fuzz to amp-like overdrive.
column10: The historic-concept lineage is part of the product story, but the 2024 retail identity is distinct. Preserve both the original-design story and the modern production object.

column7: A new Death By Audio octave-fuzz design documented as an idiosyncratic treatment of the octave-fuzz concept, with the builder's characteristic aggressive and experimental approach.
column10: Keep the Death By Audio design identity separate from generic octave-fuzz lineage. Artwork, enclosure and control layout should be captured as specimen evidence during image-verification passes.

column7: Second-generation Rumblefuzz documented in GPX's 2024 fuzz finalist list. The model designation itself establishes a generation boundary that should be preserved independently from later production variants.
column10: Do not infer the exact circuit delta between Rumblefuzz and Rumblefuzz II without primary documentation. Preserve II as a separate generation record with chronology currently anchored to 2024 coverage.

column7: Second-generation Spacerocket octave-fuzz product appearing in GPX's 2024 fuzz finalist coverage.
column10: The Roman-numeral generation label is reliable; technical differences from Spacerocket require builder-source verification before promotion.

column7: A modern interpretation of the Ibanez/Maxon MT10 Mostortion, retaining the low-to-mid-gain amp-like voice and three-band EQ while adding a Texture switch that introduces MOSFET gain-stage clipping for a more aggressive mode. First release was a 600-unit run.
column10: Keep Mofetta separate from MT10 Mostortion. The 1990 Mostortion is the historical lineage object; Mofetta is the 2024 Wampler production identity with its own enclosure, control set and clipping behavior.

column7: JHS artist-signature distortion associated with Lario Basilio and included among GPX's 2024 distortion winners. It occupies the Marshall-style / British distortion branch of the year's modern dirt catalog.
column10: Preserve the artist-signature relationship explicitly. Detailed control and lineage claims should be confirmed against JHS primary product documentation before promotion.

column7: A 2024 God City Instruments high-gain distortion identified by GPX as one of the year's notable new distortion pedals, with a strong heavy/abrasive modern identity.
column10: Treat the 2024 census appearance as a discovery anchor. Add primary builder documentation and specimen photos before locking exact control or production details.

column7: A modern high-gain preamp/distortion selected as GPX's 2024 distortion winner. It is positioned as a broad Marshall-era / golden-era gain machine rather than a direct reproduction of one retail pedal.
column10: Preserve the amp-family lineage as descriptive context. Do not turn the phrase Golden Era into a specific historical amp claim without builder documentation.

column7: A major 2024 overdrive/preamp platform that GPX describes as offering 56 amp-in-a-box choices, making the product architecture and preset/modeling layer central to its identity.
column10: The 56-model count and digital/control architecture are important identification clues. Preserve the device as a Poly Effects product rather than flattening it into a single amp-style overdrive lineage.

column7: A multi-gain machine spanning overdrive, distortion and fuzz-like harmonic/saturation textures, selected by GPX as its 2024 overdrive winner. GPX describes twelve degrees of saturation across clipping, mids, fuzz/harmonics and EQ sections.
column10: Treat the multi-domain architecture as the defining identity. Preserve the product as a Tavysh design rather than trying to force a single traditional circuit family label.

column7: Chris Buck signature valve pedal and boost platform. Contemporary 2024 coverage describes a Marshall Plexi-style tube preamp with an independent low-end-enhanced boost section.
column10: Preserve artist signature and tube-preamp architecture as product identity. Confirm production revisions and exact valve implementation from ThorpyFX primary documentation.

column7: Twin-channel tube preamp styled after the Vox AC30 Top Boost, with separate gain/volume controls per channel and shared Tone Cut, Bass and Treble controls. GPX selected it as the 2024 overdrive bronze winner.
column10: Keep ROY separate from the Lightkeeper family. The dual-channel format, tube-preamp identity and shared EQ controls are strong specimen markers.

column7: Updated re-release of the Dutch Overdrive with a Hi/Low footswitch, revised enclosure, top-mounted jacks, soft-touch switching with last-state memory and 9-18V operation. LPD describes it as a modernized return of the Dutch design.
column10: Treat Dutch '24 as a distinct revision/edition of an existing product family, not automatically as a brand-new family. The visible hardware and switching changes are valuable identification surfaces.
